plan: Given it's a single round and my value is $22, I need to balance winning with avoiding overpaying. Since values are redrawn each round, past history is irrelevant. I'll bid slightly above what I estimate the others might bid, aiming to win against likely conservative bids. A bid around $11-12 should be competitive without exceeding my value too much.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true private value, regardless of the bidding behavior of others. Bidding higher than my value could lead to a loss if the second-highest bid exceeds $18. Bidding lower than my value increases the chance of losing a profitable item. Since the values are redrawn and this is the only round, bidding exactly my value maximizes my expected profit.

Since this is round 1 of 1, and my value is only $8, I need to be very cautious. Bidding too high risks overpaying. I will bid slightly above zero, hoping to win if the other bidders are also conservative, but minimizing losses if they bid aggressively.
